basis: Beta v4 P41 (S16 country stress tests, CS TTO): in beta v3 TTO's 9.37 bn of gas exports are valued at the importers' BACI route unit values (855 USD m per bcm, 0.65 of TTF), so X - M is about 53% of GDP against about 23% implied by the WDI 2022 current account. TTO's own customs (UN Comtrade reporter 780, 2022, partner World, data/un_comtrade_rx_2022/comtrade_X_271111_2022.json) report LNG exports of 1,116.8 USD m FOB on 1.2426 Mt net weight, 899 USD/t, about 661 USD m per bcm (17.4 USD/MMBtu at 40 PJ per bcm); no 271121 record. Much of Atlantic LNG's output is sold to the train owners' affiliates at FOB or Henry Hub-linked prices, so the trading margin is booked abroad. GTAP 12 ch.12 §12.3.6 computes country-specific natural gas export prices from UN COMTRADE; the text does not say whether exporter or importer reports are used, so taking the exporter's own report for TTO (instead of the BACI importer-side value) is our reading, labelled. The reported tonnage (1.24 Mt) is far below the shipped volume (about 9-10 Mt), so only the unit value is used, on S11's volume. Alternative value: EI 2022 Henry Hub (a lower bound for an HH-linked FOB price).
